task: Run the held-out gate loop end to end against a live scorer, then act on what the run measured. The loop shipped in PR #3430 and PR #3458 had never been driven by a real model; its accept rule had only ever been exercised on synthetic mappings.

events.content: First end-to-end run of the loop against a real model. Fingerprint 06f74397...
A held-out ACCEPT, which the loop is built to treat as the win condition.
The verdict on this benchmark was decided by scorer variance, not by the edit. The real candidate got lucky; the no-op got unlucky.
489 tests pass, 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules, ruff and mypy clean.

Four blocking findings closed, verified by replaying the 2026-07-27 live runs: the false ACCEPT is now refused naming both the family bar and the corrected per-comparison bar, and attempts to loosen the bar to 0.5 or drop it are refused without spending a consultation. 508 tests pass with 100 percent line coverage on all three optimizer modules. Code landed as a5791784c.

Reported that the rule-path finding was independently corroborated on the agent benchmark: twelve of twenty-four agent fixtures moving on identical input. RETRACTED the same day and withdrawn in full. The two runs disagree on fixture_set_sha, so the corpus changed alongside the prompt and the comparison was confounded, not a null control. No valid agent-path null control exists in the repository. What survives: the rule path has a live null control, and the hook path needs none because pytest results are deterministic.
489 tests pass at this point in the session, 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules, ruff and mypy clean.

WRONG, retracted the same day in the phase below. The agent-path null control was not a null control: the two runs disagree on fixture_set_sha, so the corpus changed along with nothing else I had checked. The twelve-of-twenty-four corroboration is withdrawn in full. What survives this phase is the defect shape 16 correction, which rests on rule-path data, and the --max-p ledger verification, which does not depend on what the reports measured.

All three findings closed. The id invariant test in tests/skills/memory/test_update_causal_graph.py caught the second-order breakage before it reached the remote, which is exactly what that test exists for. 96 tests pass in that file.

A published claim is withdrawn within hours of publishing it, and the withdrawal produced a real defect: the comparison tool ignores the field the report format provides to validate the comparison. Task ids are not a substitute, since all eight ids matched while the contents differed. Corrected state of the evidence: one path, the rule path, has a valid null control; the hook path needs none because pytest_results is deterministic; the agent path has none.

1050 tests pass with 100% coverage on all three optimizer modules. Ruff and mypy clean on changed files. The guard refuses the exact pair that produced the retracted claim, and refuses it again when the envelope is stripped.

Five review findings closed, one documented overclaim corrected rather than defended. Ruff and mypy clean on changed files, no em or en dashes in any changed file.

Three round-17 findings fixed TDD and empirically re-proved. The generalizable lesson: a shared payload builder does not stop two call sites from drifting, it only makes the drift visible as an argument, so a test must assert the call sites produce equal output.
